e-4327.knowledge_point: Finding the Angle Between Two Vectors Given Their Components
e-4327.problem: Find the angle between $\mathbf{a}=\langle 2,-1,1 \rangle$ and $\mathbf{b}=\langle 1,5,-2 \rangle$. Round your answer to $1$ decimal place.
e-4327.worked_solution:
Rearranging the dot product formula, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{a\cdot b}{|\,a\,||\,b\,|} \\  & =\frac{{a}_{x}{b}_{x}+{a}_{y}{b}_{y}+{a}_{z}{b}_{z}}{\sqrt{{a}_{x}^{2}+{a}_{y}^{2}+{a}_{z}^{2}}\sqrt{{b}_{x}^{2}+{b}_{y}^{2}+{b}_{z}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{2\cdot 1+(-1)\cdot 5+1\cdot (-2)}{\sqrt{{2}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{1}^{2}}\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{5}^{2}+(-2)^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{-5}{\sqrt{6}\cdot \sqrt{30}} \\  & =\frac{-5}{\sqrt{6}\cdot \sqrt{6}\cdot \sqrt{5}} \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{5}}{6}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\theta = \arccos \left( -\dfrac{\sqrt{5}}{6} \right) \approx 111.9^\circ.
$$

e-4328.knowledge_point: Finding the Angle Between Two Vectors Given Three Points
e-4328.problem: Find $\angle BAC$ given the points $A(2,-1,-5)$, $B(-1,0,-4)$, and $C(5,1,1).$ Round your answer to $1$ decimal place.
e-4328.worked_solution:
Note that the position vectors of the points $A$, $B$, $C$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}a=⟨2,-1,-5⟩,\,b=⟨-1,0,-4⟩,\,c=⟨5,1,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

The triangle $\triangle ABC$ is shown (schematically) in the diagram below, where we denote $\angle BAC = \theta.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14040103/assets/285b8343208079181ac6036cf9ca16abc974d59b9262878ed40c0da9af5683d0.png)

First, we find the components of $\overrightarrow{AB}$ and $\overrightarrow{AC}\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =b-a \\  & =⟨-1,0,-4⟩-⟨2,-1,-5⟩ \\  & =⟨-3,1,1⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AC} & =c-a \\  & =⟨5,1,1⟩-⟨2,-1,-5⟩ \\  & =⟨3,2,6⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the cosine of the angle between $\overrightarrow{AB}$ and $\overrightarrow{AC}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{\overset{\to }{AB}\cdot \overset{\to }{AC}}{|\overset{\to }{AB}||\overset{\to }{AC}|} \\  & =\frac{-3\cdot 3+1\cdot 2+1\cdot 6}{\sqrt{(-3)^{2}+{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}}\sqrt{{3}^{2}+{2}^{2}+{6}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{-1}{\sqrt{11}\sqrt{49}} \\  & =-\frac{1}{7\sqrt{11}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\theta = \arccos \left( -\dfrac{1}{7\sqrt{11}} \right) \approx 92.5^\circ.
$$

e-5112.knowledge_point: Finding the Angle Between Two Vectors Given the Value of Their Dot Product
e-5112.problem: Given that $\mathbf{a}\cdot \mathbf{b}=-4$, find the angle between $\mathbf{a}=\langle t, \, -2 \rangle$ and $\mathbf{b}=\langle 6, \, t \rangle$. Round your answer to $1$ decimal place.
e-5112.worked_solution:
First, since $\mathbf{a}\cdot \mathbf{b}=-4$, we can solve for $t$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot b & =-4 \\ t\cdot 6+(-2)\cdot t & =-4 \\ 6t-2t & =-4 \\ 4t & =-4 \\ t & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

So, 

$$
\begin{aligned}a=⟨-1,-2⟩,\,b=⟨6,-1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the cosine of the angle between $\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{b}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{a\cdot b}{|\,a\,||\,b\,|} \\  & =\frac{{a}_{x}{b}_{x}+{a}_{y}{b}_{y}}{\sqrt{{a}_{x}^{2}+{a}_{y}^{2}}\sqrt{{b}_{x}^{2}+{b}_{y}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{-4}{\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+(-2)^{2}}\cdot \sqrt{{6}^{2}+(-1)^{2}}} \\  & =-\frac{4}{\sqrt{5}\cdot \sqrt{37}} \\  & =-\frac{4}{\sqrt{185}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\theta = \arccos \left( -\dfrac{4}{\sqrt{185}} \right) \approx 107.1^\circ.
$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{DE} & =⟨{3}^{2}-3,-3,3-3⟩ \\  & =⟨6,-3,0⟩, \\ \overset{\to }{DF} & =⟨3,{3}^{2}-5,-2⟩ \\  & =⟨3,4,-2⟩.\end{aligned}

$$

content.problem: Consider the points $D(t,5,3)$, $E({t}^{2},2,t)$ and $F(t+3,{t}^{2},1).$ Find $∠EDF$ given that $\overset{\to }{DE}\cdot \overset{\to }{DF}=6.$ Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.
content.worked_solution:
Note that the position vectors of the points $D$, $E$, $F$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}d=⟨t,\,5,\,3⟩,\,e=⟨{t}^{2},\,2,\,t⟩,\,f=⟨t+3,\,{t}^{2},\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

The triangle $△DEF$ is shown (schematically) in the diagram below, where we denote $∠EDF=\theta .$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14040103/assets/c9cfb3e84e6f76d243125f2a09246b2a1300a0134e71359bb2b528082f064f93.png)

First, we find the components of $\overset{\to }{DE}$ and $\overset{\to }{DF}$:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{DE} & =e-d \\  & =⟨{t}^{2},\,2,\,t⟩-⟨t,\,5,\,3⟩ \\  & =⟨{t}^{2}-t,\,-3,\,t-3⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{DF} & =f-d \\  & =⟨t+3,\,{t}^{2},\,1⟩-⟨t,\,5,\,3⟩ \\  & =⟨3,\,{t}^{2}-5,\,-2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $\overset{\to }{DE}\cdot \overset{\to }{DF}=6$, we can solve for $t$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{DE}\cdot \overset{\to }{DF} & =6 \\ ({t}^{2}-t)\cdot 3+(-3)\cdot ({t}^{2}-5)+(t-3)\cdot (-2) & =6 \\ 3{t}^{2}-3t-3{t}^{2}+15-2t+6 & =6 \\ -5t+21 & =6 \\ -5t & =-15 \\ t & =3\end{aligned}
$$

So, 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{DE} & =⟨{3}^{2}-3,-3,3-3⟩ \\  & =⟨6,-3,0⟩, \\ \overset{\to }{DF} & =⟨3,{3}^{2}-5,-2⟩ \\  & =⟨3,4,-2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, the cosine of the angle between $\overset{\to }{DE}$ and $\overset{\to }{DF}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{\overset{\to }{DE}\cdot \overset{\to }{DF}}{|\overset{\to }{DE}||\overset{\to }{DF}|} \\  & =\frac{6}{\sqrt{{6}^{2}+(-3)^{2}+{0}^{2}}\sqrt{{3}^{2}+{4}^{2}+(-2)^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{6}{3\sqrt{5}\cdot \sqrt{29}} \\  & =\frac{2}{\sqrt{145}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\theta =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(\frac{2}{\sqrt{145}})≈{80.44}^{∘}.
$$

after.worked_solution:
Note that the position vectors of the points $A,$ $B$ and $C$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}a=⟨2t,\,4,\,3⟩,\,b=⟨5t-1,\,4,\,3⟩,\,c=⟨2t+4,\,t+5,\,3⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

The triangle $△ABC$ is shown (schematically) in the diagram below, where we denote $∠BAC=\theta .$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14040103/assets/285b8343208079181ac6036cf9ca16abc974d59b9262878ed40c0da9af5683d0.png)

First, we find the components of $\overset{\to }{AB}$ and $\overset{\to }{AC}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =b-a \\  & =⟨5t-1,\,4,\,3⟩-⟨2t,\,4,\,3⟩ \\  & =⟨3t-1,\,0,\,0⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AC} & =c-a \\  & =⟨2t+4,\,t+5,\,3⟩-⟨2t,\,4,\,3⟩ \\  & =⟨4,\,t+1,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $\overset{\to }{AB}\cdot \overset{\to }{AC}=8,$ we can solve for $t,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB}\cdot \overset{\to }{AC} & =8 \\ (3t-1)\cdot 4+0\cdot (t+1)+0\cdot 0 & =8 \\ 4(3t-1)+0+0 & =8 \\ 12t-4 & =8 \\ 12t & =12 \\ t & =1\end{aligned}
$$

So, 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =⟨2,0,0⟩, \\ \overset{\to }{AC} & =⟨4,\,2,\,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, the cosine of the angle between $\overset{\to }{AB}$ and $\overset{\to }{AC}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{\overset{\to }{AB}\cdot \overset{\to }{AC}}{|\overset{\to }{AB}||\overset{\to }{AC}|} \\  & =\frac{8}{\sqrt{{2}^{2}+{0}^{2}+{0}^{2}}\cdot \sqrt{{4}^{2}+{2}^{2}+{0}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{8}{\sqrt{4}\cdot \sqrt{20}} \\  & =\frac{8}{\sqrt{80}} \\  & =\frac{8}{4\sqrt{5}} \\  & =\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\theta =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}})≈{26.57}^{∘}.
$$

Note that the position vectors of the points A, B and C are

a=⟨2t,4,3⟩,b=⟨5t−1,4,3⟩,c=⟨2t+4,t+5,3⟩.

The triangle △ABC is shown (schematically) in the diagram below, where we denote ∠BAC=θ.

First, we find the components of AB→ and AC→: AB→=b−a=⟨5t−1,4,3⟩−⟨2t,4,3⟩=⟨3t−1,0,0⟩AC→=c−a=⟨2t+4,t+5,3⟩−⟨2t,4,3⟩=⟨4,t+1,0⟩

Now, since AB→⋅AC→=8, we can solve for t, as follows:

AB→⋅AC→=8(3t−1)⋅4+0⋅(t+1)+0⋅0=84(3t−1)+0+0=812t−4=812t=12t=1

So, AB→=⟨2,0,0⟩,AC→=⟨4,2,0⟩.

cos⁡θ=AB→⋅AC→|AB→||AC→|=822+02+02⋅42+22+02=84⋅20=880=845=25.

Therefore, θ=arccos⁡(25)≈26.57∘.

content.problem: Consider the points $A(2t,4,3),$ $B(5t-1,4,3)$ and $C(2t+4,t+5,3).$ Find $∠BAC$ given that $\overset{\to }{AB}\cdot \overset{\to }{AC}=8.$ Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.
content.worked_solution:
Note that the position vectors of the points $A,$ $B$ and $C$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}a=⟨2t,\,4,\,3⟩,\,b=⟨5t-1,\,4,\,3⟩,\,c=⟨2t+4,\,t+5,\,3⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

The triangle $△ABC$ is shown (schematically) in the diagram below, where we denote $∠BAC=\theta .$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14040103/assets/285b8343208079181ac6036cf9ca16abc974d59b9262878ed40c0da9af5683d0.png)

First, we find the components of $\overset{\to }{AB}$ and $\overset{\to }{AC}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =b-a \\  & =⟨5t-1,\,4,\,3⟩-⟨2t,\,4,\,3⟩ \\  & =⟨3t-1,\,0,\,0⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AC} & =c-a \\  & =⟨2t+4,\,t+5,\,3⟩-⟨2t,\,4,\,3⟩ \\  & =⟨4,\,t+1,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $\overset{\to }{AB}\cdot \overset{\to }{AC}=8,$ we can solve for $t,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB}\cdot \overset{\to }{AC} & =8 \\ (3t-1)\cdot 4+0\cdot (t+1)+0\cdot 0 & =8 \\ 4(3t-1)+0+0 & =8 \\ 12t-4 & =8 \\ 12t & =12 \\ t & =1\end{aligned}
$$

So, 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =⟨2,0,0⟩, \\ \overset{\to }{AC} & =⟨4,\,2,\,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, the cosine of the angle between $\overset{\to }{AB}$ and $\overset{\to }{AC}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{\overset{\to }{AB}\cdot \overset{\to }{AC}}{|\overset{\to }{AB}||\overset{\to }{AC}|} \\  & =\frac{8}{\sqrt{{2}^{2}+{0}^{2}+{0}^{2}}\cdot \sqrt{{4}^{2}+{2}^{2}+{0}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{8}{\sqrt{4}\cdot \sqrt{20}} \\  & =\frac{8}{\sqrt{80}} \\  & =\frac{8}{4\sqrt{5}} \\  & =\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\theta =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}})≈{26.57}^{∘}.
$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB}\cdot \overset{\to }{AC} & =2 \\ 0\cdot 2t+3t\cdot 1+(-1)\cdot 1 & =2 \\ 3t-1 & =2 \\ 3t & =3 \\ t & =1\end{aligned}
$$

So, 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =⟨0,3,-1⟩, \\ \overset{\to }{AC} & =⟨2,\,1,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, the cosine of the angle between $\overset{\to }{AB}$ and $\overset{\to }{AC}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{\overset{\to }{AB}\cdot \overset{\to }{AC}}{|\overset{\to }{AB}||\overset{\to }{AC}|} \\  & =\frac{2}{\sqrt{{0}^{2}+{3}^{2}+(-1)^{2}}\cdot \sqrt{{2}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{2}{\sqrt{10}\cdot \sqrt{6}} \\  & =\frac{2}{2\sqrt{15}} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{15}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\theta =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(\frac{1}{\sqrt{15}})≈{75}^{∘}.
$$

$$

after.problem: Given that $a\cdot b=-5$, find the angle between $a=⟨2t,t⟩$ and $b=⟨1,3⟩.$
after.worked_solution:
First, since $a\cdot b=-5$, we can solve for $t$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot b & =-5 \\ 2t\cdot 1+t\cdot 3 & =-5 \\ 2t+3t & =-5 \\ 5t & =-5 \\ t & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

So, 

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨2(-1),\,(-1)⟩ \\  & =⟨-2,-1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the cosine of the angle between $a$ and $b$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{a\cdot b}{|\,a\,||\,b\,|} \\  & =\frac{{a}_{x}{b}_{x}+{a}_{y}{b}_{y}}{\sqrt{{a}_{x}^{2}+{a}_{y}^{2}}\sqrt{{b}_{x}^{2}+{b}_{y}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{-5}{\sqrt{(-2)^{2}+(-1)^{2}}\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{3}^{2}}} \\  & =-\frac{5}{\sqrt{5}\cdot \sqrt{10}} \\  & =-\frac{5}{5\sqrt{2}} \\  & =-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\theta =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}})={135}^{∘}.
$$

a⋅b=−52t⋅1+t⋅3=−52t+3t=−55t=−5t=−1

cos⁡θ=a⋅b|a||b|=axbx+aybyax2+ay2bx2+by2=−5(−2)2+(−1)212+32=−55⋅10=−552=−12.
